words.gloss: even to the tiny measure of a millet seed

literal: Of whatever greatness they may be, what is the use, if, even a millet-seed's measure not reflecting, another's house they enter?
translation: Of what use is any degree of greatness they may possess, if, without reflecting even to the measure of a tiny millet seed, they enter another's home with desire?
modern: எவ்வளவு பெருமை உடையவராக இருந்தாலும், தினை அளவு கூட ஆராய்ந்து பார்க்காமல் பிறனுடைய வீட்டிற்குள் (அவன் மனைவியை விரும்பி) நுழைந்தால் என்ன பயன்?
explanation: This couplet warns that no amount of power, learning, or social stature can save a person's reputation if they lack moral restraint. The phrase 'தினைத்துணையும் தேரான்' describes someone who fails to reflect on the consequences of their actions even to the tiny extent of a millet seed. 'பிறனில் புகல்' refers to entering another man's home with lustful intent toward his wife. The author emphasizes that this single, unthinking act of transgression completely nullifies all of one's accumulated greatness.
